description: Reject n<2; handle even n; write n-1=d*2^s for odd n. For each fixed reduced base a!=0, require a^d=1 or a^(d*2^j)=-1 for some 0<=j<s. Return true iff every witness passes. The full-u64 seven-witness theorem is an external finite-range premise, attributed to Jim Sinclair by the deterministic variants table at https://miller-rabin.appspot.com/. Rabin (1980) supplies the strong probable-prime background, not this witness-set provenance.
state: Odd tested n>=3; d odd; 1<=s<=63; every residue lies in [0,n); u128 holds (n-1)^2 exactly. Input is immutable and all loops have fixed bit/witness bounds.
cost: Seven witnesses, at most 64 exponent bits and 62 follow-up squarings each: O(log n) modular operations and O(1) space on fixed u64 words.
